findings.summary: The original 1/3/5 workload used separate projects and changed specialist limits instead of preserving the one-project, default four-specialist topology.
Restore trusted a caller boolean for scheduler state and did not exclude concurrent control-plane writes through the rebuild boundary.

verifiedRepairs: One browser-submitted PostgreSQL project, one specialist, and the default four-specialist limit drive each 1/3/5 cognitive scenario.
Every admitted fake-backend execution persists its exact sanitized observations through repository, outbox, SSE, and Chromium DOM order assertions.
Each cognitive limit has an over-capacity COGNITIVE_CAPACITY probe with zero backend observations.
Runner capacity counts only authoritative in-flight effect states in both PostgreSQL and in-memory repositories.
Restore holds an exclusive PostgreSQL maintenance lock from target inspection through independent projection proof, while normal writes, recovery, and outbox work take the shared lock.
A deterministic race proves a control-plane submission waits until validated restore releases maintenance.
residualRisks: The restore callback receives a trusted maintenance client and must use the maintenance-aware recovery entry point to avoid waiting on its own exclusive lock.
Capacity results are deterministic fake-backend/PVE fixture evidence, not a production provider or physical-host load guarantee.
